title: Introduce tiered burn decay and dynamic suppression windows for regression surge
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Summary: After the Feb 9 region-capacity regression we saw a correlated spike in burn-rate alerts that produced noisy, cascading pagers for low-impact routes. This ticket captures the follow-ups: implement a tiered burn-rate decay (fast decay for short spikes, slower decay for sustained burn), add per-route and per-customer burn hysteresis, and introduce dynamic suppression windows that shrink or expand based on correlated autoscaler/events and regional baseline capacity.

Why: Current burn-rate alerts treat all spikes the same and trigger immediate paging when thresholds cross. That design surfaces transient noise (short-lived queue/backpressure) and causes fatigue while still occasionally missing sustained degradations due to aggressive automatic suppression rules elsewhere. We need a nuanced approach to reduce noise without increasing mean time to detect true regressions.

Goals:
- Reduce actionable pager volume from SLO burn alerts by ~40% for low-impact routes while keeping detection time for high-impact regressions within current SLO.
- Avoid masking multi-region or long-duration capacity regressions.
- Provide observable rollback knobs and gradual rollout to monitor for missed incidents.

Proposed changes:
1) Tiered burn decay: implement multiple decay curves for burn calculation: short-window decay (30m half-life) for noise suppression, medium (2h) for normal ops, long (6h+) to capture long degradations. Routes are mapped to tiers by SLA/impact label.
2) Hysteresis & impact-weighting: require persistent burn above threshold for X minutes + weight by per-route request volume and revenue-impact to decide pager. This preserves fast alerting for critical routes.
3) Dynamic suppression windows: suppression window length adapts to correlated signals (autoscaler events, node restarts, cross-region capacity drops). If autoscaler is flapping, increase suppression; if multiple regions show correlated burn, reduce suppression.
4) Autoscaler correlation signal: add a short-lived tag to alert context when autoscaler activity coincides with burn spikes so on-call can triage and the system can apply special rules.
5) Quiet-mode for tier-3 routes: conversational opt-in where lower-priority customers are ticketed but not paged; notifications sent to on-call dashboard instead.
6) Observability: add a dedicated dashboard and regression-runbook link for each suppression policy change and add sampling traces for suppressed incidents.

Rollout plan:
- Phase A (canary; week 1): Enable tiered decay for 10% of traffic (non-critical regions/routes) with full observability. Monitor missed-detection rate and pager volume.
- Phase B (expanded; week 2-3): Expand to 50% with adjustments from signals.
- Phase C (global): Flip by route tiers after sign-off from SRE and Product.

Fallbacks/kill-switches: feature-flag per-region & global kill-switch; telemetry-only mode to validate before paging changes.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Missed long-duration regressions if suppression is too aggressive. Mitigation: long-window decay preserves sensitivity; we add cross-region correlation to avoid masking multi-region events.
- Risk: Complexity increase in alerting logic. Mitigation: centralize rules, add a policy UI and explainers for on-call shift handoff.

Acceptance criteria:
- Pager volume for low-impact routes reduced by >=35% in canary without increase in time-to-detect for high-impact routes (>95th percentile unchanged).
- Dashboard shows suppressed vs fired alerts, and at least one sample suppressed incident has a trace and explanation.
- Rollback path validated in canary (feature-flag off restores previous behavior).
